page.layout: One printed page. Main text in one column at the top with a marginal note at the left beside the first lines of the address; a centred author line and a small woodcut ornament in the middle; faint show-through from the reverse page in the background (not transcribed). Bottom of page: a catchword-like line of faint text and a small signature-like mark, which are show-through.

main_text.p:
Vos estis,
Deus est testis,
Teterrima pestis.
At tu Lector pie, vale in Domino, & ardenter precare, ut pacem largiatur pacificis; at dissidia volentes perdat. E nostro museo, 1. Mart. anno 1610.Ad Lectorē.
main_text.head: JOACHIMUS URSINUS, Anti-Jesuita.

page.notes: Marginal note at left reads "Ad Lectorem" (partly illegible, rendered as "Ad Lectorē."). The woodcut ornament in the centre has no text. Background show-through from the reverse page was ignored. Printed text in the first lines is partly blurred; "Vos estis" and "Quia" read with some doubt. The line "Quia omnis boni ordinis perturbatores." may continue on a line not fully legible. Faint lines near the bottom ("Nam quia vos ... eo ... ") are show-through and omitted.
